name: Grab
summary: Candidates report a Codility online assessment, then a live coding round at roughly LeetCode medium level, a system design round and a culture-fit or hiring-manager round. Many detailed public write-ups come from Grab's Bangalore office; Singapore reports describe a similar shape.

rounds.name: Online assessment
rounds.what: Codility test; candidates describe two or three easy to medium algorithm problems used as a screen.

rounds.name: Recruiter screen
rounds.what: Informal call on background, motivation and why Grab, plus simple behavioural questions.

rounds.name: Live coding
rounds.what: One or two data structures and algorithms problems solved live on an online coding platform.

rounds.name: System design
rounds.what: Whiteboard-style design discussion; Grab says it looks at scalability, security and monitoring, and candidates often get payments or ride-hailing prompts.

rounds.name: Culture fit and hiring manager
rounds.what: Conversation on collaboration and Grab's 4H values (Heart, Hunger, Honour, Humility), often with a deep dive into a past project.

tips: Think out loud: Grab says it values how you approach a problem as much as the answer.
Prepare one or two stories for each of the 4Hs: Heart, Hunger, Honour and Humility.
Know one past project in depth, including its weak points and how you would fix them.
Expect payment and ride-hailing flavoured design prompts, and drive the requirements yourself.
Review scalability, reliability and maintainability basics before the design round.
